models_evaluated: 33 VLMs (medical and general-purpose; individual names not given in text)

links.outcome: Lay-register quality versus expert-register quality of VLM-generated image descriptions
links.effect: Medical VLMs achieve strong expert captioning but suffer significant lay-register degradation. General-purpose VLMs produce more accessible language but lack clinical precision. Neither paradigm adequately serves patient-facing communication.
links.quote: Benchmarking 33 VLMs on MedLayXPlain-122K reveals a systematic Expert-Lay Gap: medical VLMs achieve strong expert captioning but suffer significant lay-register degradation, while general-purpose VLMs produce more accessible language yet lack clinical precision, confirming that neither current paradigm adequately serves patient-facing communication.

unlisted_practices: Ontology-verified lay caption generation pipeline (HOVER) combining vocabulary mapping, constrained LLM rewriting, and cross-model visual verification
Distilled lightweight evaluator (MedLayEval) scoring expert-lay alignment on clinically grounded attributes

screen.reason: The paper benchmarks 33 vision-language models on MedLayXPlain, an automated benchmark evaluating the expert-to-lay translation capability of medical VLMs for patient communication.
